summary.text: I explore how thoughtful interfaces can make complex ideas tangible. Working between design, code and the natural world, I build visual systems that stay calm under a lot of information.

story.text: I make digital things with clarity, curiosity and care.

My work starts with looking: at maps, at instruments, at the way light moves across a surface. From those observations I build interfaces, visual systems and small open tools that help other people look more closely too.
This is an illustrative portfolio for the Refract template. Alex Morgan, the studio history and the projects shown here are fictional examples, ready to be replaced with your own work.

projects.name: Field Notes
projects.description: A visual notebook for observing patterns in landscapes, cities and everyday life. Three years of field sketches became a searchable atlas of forms, colours and rhythms.

image.alt: Field Notes: contour lines of an invented terrain crossed by a surveyed transect

projects.name: Common Ground
projects.description: An interface study that makes complex environmental information easier to explore. Climate, land use and movement share one calm, legible reading.

image.alt: Common Ground: three layered environmental series with one annotated reading

projects.name: Open Atlas
projects.description: A small collection of open visual tools for navigating connected ideas. Every node keeps its sources, so a line of thought can be retraced and shared.

image.alt: Open Atlas: a constellation of connected nodes around a few anchors

projects.name: Material Studies
projects.description: Experiments with light, geometry and motion across physical and digital surfaces. Glass, paper and pixels are studied under the same light.

image.alt: Material Studies: a ray of light dispersed into six bands by a faceted solid
